title: Verify OpenNext Durable Object queue export after Cloudflare failover
description: Wrangler deploy warned that DOQueueHandler was not exported from the Worker, although .open-next/worker.js exports it and all workers.dev routes passed. Verify on-demand revalidation after cutover and fix bundling/export if queue errors appear.
notes:
2026-11-26: generated .open-next/worker.js exports DOQueueHandler and BucketCachePurge, and wrangler.toml now has both bindings plus migrations v1/v2. Wrangler still emits a non-fatal warning; runtime on-demand revalidation has not been directly exercised. OpenNext config now adds queueCache(doQueue, {regionalCacheTtlSec:30}) and purgeCache({type:'durableObject'}) to reduce queue/purge pressure. Keep open until an on-demand revalidation request succeeds without queue errors.
2026-11-27: Closed after live wrangler tail of POST /api/revalidate captured purgeCacheByTags, a scheduled revalidation time, and rpcMethod: revalidate with all invocations outcome ok and no exceptions. Generated worker exports DOQueueHandler/BucketCachePurge; Wrangler warning is non-fatal.

title: Monitor Workers Free limits during failover
description: Workers Free was selected for the Cloudflare failover. Monitor requests/day against 100,000 and CPU per request against 10 ms; upgrade to Workers Paid if either approaches its limit.
notes:
Telemetry review found Workers Observability Free with sample_rate=1 and a 200,000 events/day cap. A 24h sample showed ~387 requests, avg CPU 40.5 ms, p99 390 ms, max 509 ms; a later 1h probe showed 619 requests. The observed CPU metric is above the assumed 10 ms Free limit, so interpretation/billing needs verification. Use just cf-tail, just cf-tail-errors, just cf-deployments, and just cf-versions during monitoring.
2026-11-26 diagnosis: 1,633 'Worker exceeded CPU time limit.' errors, ~10,900 invocations >10 ms CPU (avg 73 ms, max 951 ms), 551 503s, 105 ISR queue revalidation failures. Root causes: uncached Worker HTML, failing ISR revalidation, no CDN caching of Worker responses, and bot/legacy 404 traffic. Hardening deployed at version a3cb274b-671a-45d3-a04a-e4186e25da4c: OpenNext cache interception + regional cache + queue dedupe + DO purge, Workers Cache enabled (cf-cache-status MISS then HIT), and middleware short-circuits for legacy paths. Verified / 200, /wp-login.php 404, /xmlrpc.php 404, x-opennext-cache HIT. A bot-UA middleware fallback is built but deployment is blocked on Cloudflare OAuth re-auth. Post-hardening telemetry read APIs return 503/10001 or 504 for current credentials; keep this issue open until new CPU/error trend is observed.
2026-11-26 follow-up: user chose to stop before redeploying the built scraper-UA middleware. Live Worker remains a3cb274b-671a-45d3-a04a-e4186e25da4c (cache hardening only). Bot-UA deploy deferred as medialternatives-ghv; WAF rules blocked as medialternatives-esx. Continue monitoring CPU/error trend and close only after a clean post-hardening window.
2026-11-27: Wrangler OAuth access restored. Deployed bot-UA middleware as version 65910e4d-9af6-4927-92ce-b918dcb89a8b; PetalBot/ClaudeBot with cache-busting query now return 403, normal UA 200, /wp-login.php 404. Live tail of 7 forced-uncached requests: all outcome ok, avg CPU 67.4 ms, p50 34 ms, max 233 ms; all exceeded 10 ms because query strings bypassed cache. Repeated fixed URLs show cf-cache-status HIT and produce no Worker invocation, which is the intended CPU savings. WAF/ruleset API still 403 with OAuth token and MCP token remains invalid; WAF work remains medialternatives-esx.
2026-11-27: WAF edge protection is live. Live tail during 10 WAF-blocked requests showed zero Worker invocations; the single cache-busting normal request returned ok at 16 ms CPU. Keep open for a longer real-traffic CPU/error trend.
2026-11-27: Closed after Cloudflare GraphQL analytics showed zero exceededResources/CPU-limit errors across 17,199 Worker invocations from 2026-11-26T16:00Z to 2026-11-27T15:17Z. Last CPU-limit error hour was 2026-11-26T15:00Z. Workers Cache and WAF edge blocks remove most traffic from the Worker runtime; continue periodic monitoring.
